head_commit.message:
ci: let both claude review lanes post inline pr comments (#923)

The workflow has always told Claude to "post findings as inline comments
on the changed lines" and neither lane could. At the pinned action SHA the
inline-comment MCP server only starts when allowedTools names something
with the mcp__github_inline_comment__ prefix, and tag mode's own list is
Glob/Grep/LS/Read plus the comment-update and CI tools. So the instruction
was a silent no-op and findings landed in the tracking comment instead.

Name the tool in both lanes. Agent mode gates on the same prefix check, so
the automatic gate gets it too - capped by the prompt to blocking findings
only (HIGH/CRITICAL, confidence >= 0.8, introduced_by_diff), since that
lane re-runs on every synchronize and inline comments are not deduplicated
across runs. The threshold matches ci-review-verdict.mjs so the inline
comments and the red check cannot disagree.

The two comment blocks explaining why inline posting "worked" were both
wrong; replaced with the real mechanism and source citations so the next
action bump can be re-verified. ADR-0008 repeated the same wrong claim
twice and is corrected.

head_commit.message:
chore: add robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt to the landing site (#922)

* chore: add robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt to the landing site

The static site shipped with no crawl metadata at all: no robots.txt, no
sitemap, and nothing aimed at LLM crawlers.

- robots.ts allows everything except /mission-control (a live GitHub-API
  dashboard that already sets robots index false on the page) and points at
  the sitemap.
- sitemap.ts lists the 8 indexable routes, matching each page's own canonical.
  No lastModified/priority: Google ignores priority and a build-time timestamp
  would churn the file on every deploy.
- public/llms.txt follows the llms.txt convention (H1, summary blockquote, key
  facts, Pages, Optional). Adoption by AI crawlers is currently unproven, but
  the file is static and costs one bullet per new page.

Both metadata routes need a force-static dynamic export: Next 16 defaults them
to dynamic and output export rejects that outright.

Verified: typecheck, build (out/robots.txt + out/sitemap.xml + out/llms.txt all
emitted), check:parity, and lint:strict --max-warnings 0 all pass.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix: keep /mission-control crawlable so its noindex is readable

Review findings on #922 (frontend-reviewer, all advisory).

MEDIUM: the robots.txt Disallow on /mission-control cancelled the page-level
noindex instead of reinforcing it. A crawler that obeys Disallow never fetches
the page, so it never reads the noindex, and the bare URL stays indexable from
external links — the exact outcome noindex prevents. Dropped the rule; the
comment now explains why the page must stay fetchable.

LOW: /how-it-works and /creature shipped without a canonical, so the invariant
asserted in sitemap.ts held for only 6 of 8 routes. Added both, matching the
other six pages.

LOW: added robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt to the existing REQUIRED_FILES
list in check-parity.mjs. Three entries in machinery that already runs in CI,
and it catches the failure the PR itself documents: if the force-static export
is dropped or Next changes metadata-route defaults, the build stops emitting
these files silently. Verified the guard bites by removing out/robots.txt —
check:parity fails with the expected message, passes once restored.

Verified: typecheck, build, check:parity, lint:strict --max-warnings 0.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
refactor: split the remaining ported landing bodies into sections (#920)

HowItWorksBody.tsx (340 lines), PrivacyBody.tsx (327) and CreatureBody.tsx
(262) were the last oversized files in apps/landing - all three pure static
JSX ported from hand-authored HTML with no hooks, handlers or logic.

They split verbatim into sections/ directories beside each body, cutting at
the markup's own structural units: how-it-works at its <aside> and #view-*
sections, privacy at its <h2>-delimited blocks, creature at doodles, stage
and overlays. The shells are 38, 25 and 24 lines.

No JSX was rewritten, matching the approach used for the home files in #917.
Verified against pre-split builds: tag sequence with ids and classes and
whitespace-collapsed visible text are both byte-identical on all three pages
(189/23474, 191/15134, 94/10560).

The inline-hex eslint exemption gains creature/sections/**, scoped rather
than a creature/** glob so the directory stays covered by the brand-token
rule if a hand-written file lands there. All 14 new files are added to
SECRET_SCAN_FILES, which fails open for anything unlisted.

Provenance headers on the privacy sections no longer claim privacy-0.js
binds to the page; it is a console easter egg with no DOM binding, and
check-parity is what actually pins that page. Corrected on PrivacyBody.tsx
too, where the claim originated.

head_commit.message:
refactor: split agent-fleet into sections and pure scroll modules (#916)

AgentFleet.tsx was 830 lines: six page sections, three scroll-driven effects,
and a component defined inside the render body.

Pure math moves to lib/agent-system: links.ts holds the bezier geometry,
belt.ts the scrub progress and nearest-station argmin, reveal.ts the count-up
easing and scene clamp, clipboard.ts the copy helper. The hardcoded /9 at
three sites becomes STATION_COUNT derived from STATIONS.length, and the
breakpoint, debounce, duration and threshold literals are named constants.

The three effects become useMapLinks, useBeltScrub and useReveal in hooks.ts,
each keeping its own rAF flag and listener teardown. Markup splits into six
section components plus Glyph, Machine, Divider, Station and NodeButton.
Hero coords, divider paths, legend rows, team lists and the save-job prompt
move to data/agent-fleet.ts as additive exports.

NodeButton is hoisted from the render body to module scope. This is the one
non-behavior-preserving change: it previously got a fresh component identity
every render, so React unmounted and remounted it, restarting focus and
transitions. It now takes name, roleClass, selected, onSelect and onHover.

State follows its markup - route into IntakeSection, selected and litName into
FleetMapSection - leaving AgentFleet.tsx at 29 lines with no prop drilling.
